name: KAS Glute Bridge
instructions: Sit on the floor with your back against a bench and a barbell over your hips with padding.
Place your feet flat, knees bent.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Lower only partway so tension stays on the glutes, then repeat.
longevityNotes: Hip-hinge strength protects the lower back in every lift, from groceries to grandchildren. Strong glutes and hamstrings are the engine of walking, climbing, and standing up.
overview: A barbell glute bridge in the KAS (Kinetic Alignment Standard) style that keeps constant tension on the glutes with a partial range.
